name: CA-31
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Gil Cisneros holds a D+8 district with a roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge ($853k to $97k) and a large cash-on-hand lead
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No public general-election polling exists, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and a favorable environment
Challenger Eric Ching has only about $10,000 on hand and no outside support on record
model.rationale: Cisneros combines an eight-point Democratic district, incumbency, and an overwhelming financial advantage, while markets price his reelection near 96 percent; with no polling suggesting otherwise, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Ching or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow the expected margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 31st District leans Democratic by eight points, and incumbent Gil Cisneros enters the general election with every visible advantage. He has raised roughly $853,000 to Eric Ching's $97,000, holds a wide cash-on-hand edge, and is the only candidate benefiting from recorded outside spending. Prediction markets put his chances near 96 percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals: the partisan lean, Cisneros's incumbency, and a favorable environment. Ching, a local official, would need a dramatic shift in the political climate or an influx of outside money to become competitive. As structured, the race ranks among the safer Democratic holds this cycle, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
